messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] service=inference-runtime-prod severity=SEV2 — spike in 5xx and request timeouts, several model-runner pods crashed (OOM / SIGSEGV). Auto-runbook: <https://runbooks.internal/inf-runtime#faultwave|faultwave>
jamie (oncall): paging in, joining bridge. can someone grab errors/regions? :wave:
alex (infra): looks like eu-west-1 is hit hardest, ~12% 5xx for the last 10min. alert shows node-level OOMs on model-runner pods.
priya (runtime): attaching quick logs snip from runner-logs:

```
[2026-03-17T11:05:21Z] model-runner[pid=3021]: segfault at 0x7ffc..., pc 0x55a1d3f4
[2026-03-17T11:05:23Z] OOM killer invoked: python3 (model-triton)
[2026-03-17T11:05:25Z] healthcheck: unhealthy -> 503
```

priya (runtime): repro is intermittent under longer contexts (>=2048 tokens). suspect kv-cache growth + quant kernel mem bug.
maya (sre): creating mitigation plan: 1) route traffic away from eu-west-1 to us-east-1 canaries, 2) pin requests to fallback-small model for affected customers, 3) scale down max seq length for realtime routes.
jamie (oncall): make the changes and post commands here. keeping bridge open. ops-bot: start customer-impact notice draft.
ops-bot: DRAFT: "We are investigating elevated errors impacting inference in EU region; routing mitigations in progress. No data loss." Will post after confirmation.
alex (infra): routing change (manual weight adjust) issued: `kubectl patch svc inference-gateway -p '{"spec":{"trafficPolicy":{"weights":{"eu-west-1":0.25}}}}'` — reducing EU weight to 25% while we validate.
luke (support): customers with heavy traffic on eu-west-1 seeing 502/503; I started a ticket for top 5 impacted accounts and flagged for SEs.
priya (runtime): quick hot-mitigation: disable kv-cache for model-runner on the affected node pool, command:

```
kubectl -n infra set env daemonset/model-runner KV_CACHE_ENABLED=false --all
```

priya (runtime): doing a rolling restart on the node-pool after env flip to ensure clean memory: `kubectl rollout restart ds/model-runner -n infra`.
jamie (oncall): good. track request success rate. maya, can you validate no regressions on latency when routing to fallback-small?
maya (sre): confirmed: fallback-small latency +40ms but 5xx drops to <1%. pushing canary for all realtime routes.
alex (infra): observed one worker crash during restart with stacktrace; uploading to debug link: <https://logs.internal/616162/segfault-attach>
priya (runtime): root cause hypothesis: quantized attention kernel under long context triggers an invalid read causing segfault then OOM when recycled. will open a runtime patch PR to add bounds check + fallback to non-quant kernel.
jamie (oncall): what's ETA on patch? can we hotfix or do we need rollout with fallback config?
priya (runtime): hotfix PR ready, need a canary build validation (~20m) then rolling deploy. plan B: keep KV_CACHE disabled and use fallback-small for high-context requests until patch is live.
luke (support): customers updated: posted to affected accounts and support queue. asking for estimated resolution time (ETA) ~45-60m.
ops-bot: CUSTOMER NOTICE (post): "We're mitigating elevated errors in EU region. We've rerouted traffic and applied temporary mitigations. Expect intermittent availability for long-context requests. We'll update in 30 minutes or on progress."
jamie (oncall): assigning action owners: priya=runtime patch + deploy, alex=network routing + node restarts, maya=monitoring + rollback plan, luke=customer comms. keep each update brief.
priya (runtime): deploying canary build to 2 pods now.
priya (runtime): canary logs look clean for 15m, no OOMs; proceeding with gradual rollout.
alex (infra): traffic weight back to eu-west-1 at 70% with fallback rules for >1024 token requests -> routed to fallback-small.
maya (sre): metrics: 5xx rate dropped from 12% -> 1.1% in eu-west-1 after mitigations. tail latency stable.
jamie (oncall): nice work. closing bridge once rollout hits 100% and we hold for 30m. update final post for customers.
priya (runtime): rollout completed at +36m. monitoring for 2 hours.
luke (support): updating tickets: ETA updated to resolved in 2h, customers appreciative of quick mitigation. :thumbsup:
jamie (oncall): incident summary to be filed to postmortems later. please add timestamps and PR link. incident-bot, mark incident resolved when monitors stable.
incident-bot: Monitor check passed — error rate stable for 30m. Marking as RESOLVED (SEV2 -> RESOLVED). Reference: INC-616162
